_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present and fails CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: account-alerts-open / account-alerts-resolved key on `alert_uid` (the API's camelCase `alertUid`) in resourceIDFieldOverrides, in BOTH the sync extractor and the store extractor
handfixes.why: Datto RMM alert objects carry no id/uid/uuid/name/slug/key/code field -- `alertUid` is the only identifier (see internal/types.Alert). Every entry in genericIDFieldFallbacks therefore misses, and suffixIDFieldFallback cannot help either: it derives probes from the RESOURCE name ("account-alerts-open" -> "account-alerts-open_id"), never the "alert" stem, and matches by direct snake_case map lookup so it would never see camelCase `alertUid` regardless. Result before this override: sync consumed every alert and stored zero, emitting sync_anomaly all_items_failed_id_extraction (250/0), leaving local alert search and fleet analytics silently blind. Reported by @zendzipr in #258. The override map is duplicated in internal/cli/sync.go and internal/store/store.go -- both must carry it; fixing only one restores the silent drop. 4.34.2 reprint: now spec-encoded (x-resource-id alert_uid on the six alert list paths, tools/spec_fix.py), so the generator emits both override lines itself; the asserts still pin them.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: The durable fix is upstream: the press profiler should set IDField from the response-item schema when the item declares exactly one identifier-shaped field (`<stem>Uid`/`<stem>Id`) and no generic id. Filed as a /printing-press-retro item. Until the press emits it, or the Datto spec carries x-resource-id on /v2/account/alerts/{open,resolved}, this ledger entry is what survives a reprint.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For datto-rmm the manifest gained: DATTO_RMM_BASE_URL, DATTO_RMM_PLATFORM. server.json gained: DATTO_RMM_BASE_URL, DATTO_RMM_PLATFORM. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: DATTO_RMM_BASE_URL, DATTO_RMM_PLATFORM. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: DATTO_RMM_NO_CONFIG_WRITE makes every credential write a no-op (the automatic token cache included) while leaving the `auth logout` erase working, and the MCP server honours it too (issue #270)
handfixes.why: Issue #270, raised by @Xenith-B off the back of #266. #266 stopped env-supplied client credentials reaching disk; the MINTED access token still landed in ~/.config/<tool>-cli/config.toml in cleartext and there was no supported way to turn that off. Their workaround was `--config NUL`, which is OS-specific, undocumented, makes doctor report a false 'not configured', and - the part that matters most - does not cover the MCP servers at all, because internal/mcp resolved its own hardcoded config path and ignored --config. PR #309 covered 12 connectors; this connector was one of the three auto-persisters it missed (EnsureDattoToken's best-effort SaveTokens on every OAuth mint, internal/config/datto_oauth.go). Three deliberate boundaries make this switch honest rather than merely quiet. (1) ClearTokens keeps calling save() directly: it is the ERASE path, and routing it through the guard would make `auth logout` silently inert, which is a worse defect than the one being fixed. (2) `auth login` and `auth set-token`, the two commands on this connector that write a credential on purpose, REFUSE and name the variable rather than reporting a save that did not happen - a false success is the same defect class as a doctor that says credentials are fine without checking. (3) The MCP server runs this same config package, so it honours the switch (its config-path resolution is a separate ledger entry, mcp-config-resolves-like-the-cli). The variable is declared on all three install channels because for a Claude Desktop install the manifest prompt is the ONLY channel that can set an environment variable. The tests prove both directions: under the switch the real persistence route (EnsureDattoToken against a local OAuth token double) updates the in-memory value and leaves the file absent (or byte-identical when one already exists); with the switch unset or any falsey spelling the bytes written are identical to before. Class C, new documented surface. GENERATOR-class: a reprint drops the switch entirely and silently restores the plaintext token cache.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit <PREFIX>_NO_CONFIG_WRITE (or an equivalent) as part of the standard config surface, with the same three boundaries: the erase path exempt, explicit save commands failing loudly rather than no-oping, and every best-effort auto-persist route (OAuth mint, JWT exchange, cookie rotation) routed through the single gated writer.

asserts.contains: | `auth set-token` | Refuses, naming the variable, instead of reporting a save that did not happen. |

handfixes.summary: The MCP server resolves its config through config.Load("") - honouring DATTO_RMM_CONFIG and DATTO_RMM_NO_CONFIG_WRITE exactly like the CLI - instead of a hardcoded ~/.config/datto-rmm-cli/config.toml (issue #270)
handfixes.why: Issue #270 (@Xenith-B): internal/mcp/tools.go built the config path by hand - filepath.Join(home, ".config", "datto-rmm-cli", "config.toml") - and passed it to config.Load, so the MCP server ignored DATTO_RMM_CONFIG entirely. That made --config / DATTO_RMM_CONFIG inert for every MCP install: a Claude Desktop operator had no way to point the server at a different config file, and no way to keep it away from a plaintext token cache under the home directory. newMCPClient now calls config.Load(""), the same resolver the CLI uses (root.go newClient), which reads DATTO_RMM_CONFIG, falls back to the identical default path, and applies DATTO_RMM_NO_CONFIG_WRITE (ledger entry no-config-write-switch). The test seeds a config at a non-default path, points DATTO_RMM_CONFIG at it, and asserts the MCP client's Config.Path and base_url come from that file - the exact scenario the hardcoded path broke. GENERATOR-class: the press template still hardcodes the path, so a reprint restores the defect while go build and go test stay green; this entry is what notices.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should generate newMCPClient (and the platform-bound newMCPConfig variant) with config.Load("") rather than a hand-built home-relative path; the hardcoded path is a generator defect that makes <PREFIX>_CONFIG inert for every MCP install on every connector.

handfixes.summary: `workflow archive` reports the number of resources that actually succeeded and exits non-zero when 0 of N did; partial success stays exit 0 (issue #275 finding 3, upstream #4410)
handfixes.why: DONE UPSTREAM: mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#4410 merged 2026-08-28 (28c43fa9), first shipped press v4.31.3 (2026-08-30). Issue #275 finding 3 (@Xenith-B): `workflow archive` reported `"resources_synced": len(resources)` and returned nil even when every resource errored or warned, so the JSON summary and the human line (`Archived 0 items across N resources`) were success-shaped for a tenant whose every request 401ed, and an agent reading them believed the archive was complete. This is the fleet backport of the upstream template diff (channel_workflow.go.tmpl): count resourcesSynced, report it in both surfaces, print the human summary only when something succeeded or nothing was attempted, and fail closed with `workflow archive failed: 0 of %d resource(s) archived` when 0 of N succeeded. The three outcomes are pinned by workflow_archive_outcome_test.go, which drives the real root command against a local HTTP double with dummy credentials: every resource 401 -> non-zero exit naming `0 of N resource(s) archived`, resources_synced 0, and no success-shaped summary; one resource serving rows and the rest 401 -> exit 0 with resources_synced 1 (the TRUE count) and the per-resource errors on stderr; every resource serving an empty page -> exit 0 with every attempted resource counted. Partial success stays exit 0, matching sync's default non-strict policy. This connector is on press 4.24.0, below the first fixed release, so a reprint from the vendored engine REINTRODUCES the false success while go build and go test stay green; this entry is what notices. Retire it after a reprint from press >= 4.31.3.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: None: the fix is in the press template since 4.31.3. A reprint from >= 4.31.3 regenerates it; keep the behavioural test, which is a hand-authored (NOVEL) file regen-merge preserves.

asserts.contains: return fmt.Errorf("workflow archive failed: 0 of %d resource(s) archived", len(resources))

handfixes.summary: export --output closes its output file (through the credential kit) on every return, including an API error: the open no longer shadows RunE's named err
handfixes.why: The generated `f, err := openExportOutput(...)` inside the --output block declared a new err, so the deferred close tested that inner (nil) err and never ran when the export returned an API error. Fleet note: every connector that took the ported chokepoint edit on export.go carries the same shadowing. Ported to datto from the gradient 4.34.2 reprint (one credential layer across the fleet). handfixes.summary: Every API client the CLI, the novel commands and the MCP server build mints the Datto RMM bearer from DATTO_RMM_API_KEY + DATTO_RMM_API_SECRET_KEY on first use (password grant, Basic public-client:public) through its own pinned transport; never under --dry-run or the verifier; DATTO_RMM_TOKEN wins over minting
handfixes.why: PUBLISHED REGRESSION: the 4.22 library minted in root.go newClient; the 4.24 reprint (published 0.1.8 / 0.1.10) lost that edit, so a key and secret alone answered 401 on every API command and every MCP tool until the operator ran `auth login` by hand, and the README's 'mints for you' was false. Restored as a registerClientHook (internal/cli/datto_guard.go mintForClient), which reaches every client the generated CLI and MCP constructors build, so a regeneration cannot drop it again.

handfixes.summary: DATTO_RMM_PLATFORM (or DATTO_RMM_API_URL) chooses the base URL inside config.Load and counts as an explicit base URL wherever config.go read DATTO_RMM_BASE_URL (the final override, the untrusted-route unblock, the credential target); an unknown platform refuses to load; DATTO_RMM_BASE_URL wins, then DATTO_RMM_API_URL
handfixes.why: PUBLISHED REGRESSION: the 4.24 print applied DATTO_RMM_PLATFORM only in `auth login`, so an account on pinotage minted its token on pinotage and then sent it to the merlot default on every API call (401, and a credential sent to another Datto platform). Two anchored edits in the generated config.go (tools/apply_edits.py) over hand functions in internal/config/datto_oauth.go.

handfixes.summary: A minted token is recorded with a binding (32 hex digits: a fingerprint of the API host and one of the API key, saved as the credential store's client_id) and sent only for that binding: one mint per binding per process, a stored token reused only for the same key and host, another key mints its own; with no key configured, a stored minted token is dropped when its binding names another host (a token `auth set-token` saved has no binding and stays the operator's choice)
handfixes.why: Work-order host pinning and the action1/appdirect class 'cached authentication ignores credential override': 0.1.10's `auth login` saved one token to config.toml with no record of the key or platform it came from, so switching DATTO_RMM_API_KEY or DATTO_RMM_PLATFORM sent the old token with the new key or to the new host. The binding holds no part of the key and no separator (it is held as a credential-named value and must not read as a word or a host).

handfixes.summary: The token request goes only to <API host>/auth/oauth/token over a client that follows no redirect and refuses any other host (NewDattoTokenClient, used by the mint hook and `auth login`); the fixed public client is added beneath the credential kit, so the word public is never a held value; a base URL with userinfo, a non-http scheme or a non-ASCII host mints nothing; the error text never repeats the server's answer
handfixes.why: Work-order credential rule (host pinning). 0.1.10's MintDattoToken used a default http.Client, which re-sends a 307/308 POST body (the API key and secret) to whatever host the Location names.

handfixes.summary: The local SQLite store is named by the API host and key binding (config.StoreScopeIdentity), not by the bearer token, so a re-minted token (about every 100 hours, or every run under DATTO_RMM_NO_CONFIG_WRITE) keeps the same store and the fleet analytics keep their synced data
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.2 scopes the default store file by a hash of the credential in effect (AuthHeader first), so every new token opened a new, empty data-<hash>.db: after a re-mint every fleet analytic read nothing, silently. StoreScopeIdentity is the press's own lever for 'a print whose session token rotates'.

handfixes.summary: Every sync partition walks Datto's pageDetails.nextPageUrl as a cursor (only its page value is kept; the request goes to the configured host) and asks max=250 (activity-logs: size=250); only a null next link ends a walk, so a server page cap below the requested size never truncates the copy or marks it complete for pruning
handfixes.why: Vendor-documented shape (spec PaginationData {count,totalCount,prevPageUrl,nextPageUrl}). The springdoc spec puts the page schemas under 401/403 only, so neither 4.24 nor 4.34.2 detects the next link or the max param: 0.1.10 sent limit=100 (ignored) and stored only the first page of every list (an MSP with more devices than one page saw a partial fleet in every analytic); the raw 4.34.2 render would also skip page 1 (its page-int fallback asks page=2 after an implicit page 0). tools/apply_edits.py rewrites the 17 page cases of determinePaginationDefaults.

handfixes.summary: sync keeps the 0.1.10 partition names: account = /v2/account/sites (the name every fleet analytic reads as sites), account-components = /v2/account/components; activity-logs stays in the default sync (fleet device-timeline reads it)
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.2 ranks a group's sync candidates by endpoint name and re-pointed `account` from sites to components (sites became `account-sites`), and dropped /v2/activity-logs from the default sync. An upgraded store would then hold components under the name the novels read as sites. tools/resource_names.py renames partition identifiers inside the name-keyed sync maps only (press-traps s6, the acronis class).

handfixes.summary: Synced account users key on username (x-resource-id on /v2/account/users), so sync stores every user instead of 0 of N

Spec-encoded (tools/spec_fix.py), so it survives every reprint.

handfixes.summary: The most explicit credential names the identity and nothing stored stands in for it: an environment DATTO_RMM_TOKEN is the bearer (a stored access token and a stored auth_header are dropped from the loaded config); a configured API key, with or without its secret, allows only a token minted for that key on this host (a token bound to another key or to none, a stored auth_header and a stored rmm_token are dropped)
handfixes.why: Codex review r1 class credential identity mismatch (P1): the binding was checked only when the secret was also set, so DATTO_RMM_API_KEY=key-B alone sent key A's stored token; the generated AuthHeader preferred a stored access token (or a file auth_header) over DATTO_RMM_TOKEN, so account A's token went out while DATTO_RMM_TOKEN named account B.

handfixes.summary: A sync partition serves and receives only the records of its own sync path: a generated read whose path is a sync path uses that partition, a read naming a sync partition of another path has no local read and no write-through cache, and a mutation response never enters a sync partition
handfixes.why: Codex review r1 class wrong local partition (P1): every generated account command named the one `account` partition (the synced /v2/account/sites every fleet analytic reads as sites), so `account get-user-devices --data-source local` returned sites and `account create-variable` wrote a variable into the sites partition. Hand file internal/cli/datto_partitions.go plus four anchored lines in data_source.go (tools/apply_edits.py EDITS3).

handfixes.why: Codex review r1 class documented field type misread (P1): fleet device-timeline read site and user as strings, so every real activity failed to decode and was skipped silently. handfixes.summary: `fleet sync-gaps` reports a partition whose last sync attempt did not finish (sync_state.last_attempt_complete = 0, or never completed) as incomplete, whatever its counts say; a complete sync still reads as ok
handfixes.why: Codex review r1 class incomplete sync reported healthy (P1): the recorded count is the count of rows sync stored, so a sync that stopped before the documented next page showed no drift and read as ok with no gaps.

handfixes.summary: Antivirus and patch posture read Datto's documented enums: one normalizer (letters and digits only) so --status not-running matches NotRunning; av-gaps refuses a --status that is no documented status; a device is patched only with patchStatus FullyPatched and no pending or not-approved patch
handfixes.why: Codex review r1 class documented enum misread (P1): av-gaps normalized not-running to 'not running' and never matched Datto's NotRunning; scorecard counted a NoData device (zero counters, nothing known) as patched.

handfixes.summary: The fleet analytics read one record per alertUid across the open and resolved partitions, and a resolved record wins
handfixes.why: Codex review r1 class one record counted in two partitions (P1): an alert synced while open keeps its open row until a full sync prunes it and sits in the resolved partition once resolved; the partitions were concatenated, so it counted twice in storms and as open on the scorecard.

handfixes.summary: README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json say the ChatGPT desktop app runs this connector locally (STDIO) and that ChatGPT on the web, Microsoft 365 Copilot / Copilot Studio and the Gemini app are not supported by msp-skills yet, with a link to the hosted-gateway comparison; no paid-plan list, no Developer Mode recipe, no 'ChatGPT connects only to remote servers'.

README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json are regenerated by msp-skills-publish onboard.py, whose template still writes the old ChatGPT text, so without this entry a re-onboard or reprint silently restores it.

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand and replaces the print's own credential layer (held set, encodings, output chokepoint, secret funnel, outbound and split checks, origin pin, store and journal refusals). internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal; each main starts with credkit.Start and ends with credkit.Exit; every API client gets the kit transport through the client hook (cli/credkit_client.go), and the feedback, webhook and token clients build theirs on it; every held value goes only to the API base URL this process uses; every file write outside the 0600 credential store and config goes through the kit; the store opens SQLite through credkit.SQLDriver; the MCP server passes MCPTools, MCPIn, MCPOut and MCPHTTP and runs CLI children through RunCommand.
handfixes.why: One contract, one matcher and one set of sinks replace the connector-only layer, and a matcher fix reaches this connector by vendoring. A reprint regenerates every sink, so each wiring point is asserted here. Kept honest by the built-binary tests in internal/credwire, each seen failing with its wiring point removed.

handfixes.summary: export hands the credential kit whole records: no bufio.Writer over stdout, the --deliver tee or the kit file Writer. JSON-lines records are batched by exportRecords, --format json is one Write of the whole document, and the table printers go through a tabwriter over wholeLines, so each table line is one Write. TestNoChunkingWritersOverKitSinks fails on any chunking writer in the module outside the vendored kit.
handfixes.why: The press export wrote through a 4096-byte bufio.Writer, so every unit the kit checked ended inside a record. Past the kit's 16 KiB window the stream is lost and every later unit is withheld, so an ordinary export of a few hundred sites stopped after 20 KiB. Found on backup-radar; the same press writer shipped here.

handfixes.summary: A saved run profile is a credential source: at startup, inside credkit.Start, holdProfiles reads the current profiles.json under the default home and every --home and the legacy ~/.datto-rmm-cli/profiles.json, member by member so every duplicate key is seen, and holds each base-url value's password and query values (credkit.HoldURL) and each credential flag's value (credkit.Hold). Origins sends both sources nowhere.
handfixes.why: Kit rule 8(c). Before this neither store was read at startup, so profile show printed a saved password.

handfixes.summary: DATTO_RMM_PLATFORM and DATTO_RMM_API_URL choose the API host, and the kit reads only BaseURL.Env: showBaseURL sets DATTO_RMM_BASE_URL for the length of credkit.Start when unset, and AfterStart clears it, so the kit's allowed origin is the host the program really uses.
handfixes.why: Without it a run on the zinfandel platform was refused its own host (seen failing, TestPlatformRoutesCredentialsToItsHost).

handfixes.summary: The learn journal keeps no text the operator typed in place of a declared name: the <PREFIX>_LEARN_SESSION override is stored as "o:" plus the same 64-bit SHA-256 hash the harness session ids get under "h:"; argv_shape records only flag names the invoked command declares (any other is a placeholder, nothing after "--" is a flag); the failed flag is an opaque identity; teach.log records counts, not raw arguments. A stored value that repeats a held credential is the shared credential kit's job now (credkit-wiring: every file and SQLite write goes through it).
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 and 4.34.2 (learn/journal.go.tmpl) return the override raw from JournalSessionKey, so a credential set there is written to journal-*.jsonl on every command, version included, and record every typed flag name, so a credential typed as a flag name (or after --) becomes an argv_shape key and the failed_flag; teach.log records the raw arguments of a teach with no --query; and a credential given as a profile name or description, a recall or teach query or operand, or feedback is stored as typed. Known limits: a guessable override or typed name can be confirmed by hashing guesses; entries an older build wrote stay until the 14-day retention deletes their segment; operator-named text that repeats no credential the process holds is a name and is kept. A reprint that drops these edits fails these asserts and TestJournalCredentialHardening; re-run tools/maintainer/apply_journal_hardening.py --slug <slug>. 2026-11-04 kit adoption: the RefuseHeld checks at each store and file (held_persist.go) are retired, replaced by the shared credential kit's file and SQLite sinks; the journal-shape asserts stay. Test: learn/journal_credential_hardening_test.go (the held pass holds through credkit.Hold).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: learn/journal.go.tmpl should hash the LEARN_SESSION override as it hashes harness ids, and JournalArgvShape should take the invoked command's declared-flag lookup and record any other name as a placeholder, stopping at "--"; the failed flag should be an opaque identity; teach.log should not echo raw arguments; and every template that stores operator-named text should refuse one that repeats a held credential.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

handfixes.summary: the adaptive limiter's blind ramp raises only a rate the last Wait slept on, so sync's rate_rps reports a real pace
handfixes.why: On a header-less API the ramp multiplied the rate by 1.25 every 10 successes with no ceiling: mcp2's hubspot sync printed rate_rps 6.6e24 (about 2,500 requests), and after such a ramp a 429's halving could no longer slow a single request. A rate the requests never reach is no longer raised. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe limiter-paced).
